title: LinkedIn Uses OpenTelemetry to Trace the Member Journey from Tap to Backend
gist: LinkedIn built an OpenTelemetry-based platform linking iOS, Android and web client interactions to backend traces, using a pageForestId grouping above standard traces, Kafka transport and ClickHouse storage. Coordinated head sampling and debug-tiering (up to 90% of some backend tracing volume) control cost, and the design avoids lock-in to commercial observability backends like Datadog and New Relic.

insights.claim: LinkedIn built an OpenTelemetry-based telemetry platform that lets a member interaction in its iOS, Android, and web apps be followed through frontend and backend services down to the underlying data stores.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Large-scale adoption validates OpenTelemetry as the standard foundation for end-to-end observability.

insights.claim: Historically, connecting client analytics with backend tracing required engineers to correlate separate systems, which is the observability gap LinkedIn's approach aims to close.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Unified client-to-backend tracing is a demand driver for observability tooling.

insights.claim: LinkedIn introduced a pageForestId that groups related requests from the same page context above individual OpenTelemetry traceIds, because conventional distributed tracing follows one request while a member journey involves many.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: A higher-level journey abstraction shows where standard tracing falls short and where vendors may differentiate.
insights.quote: conventional distributed tracing generally follows one request, whereas a member journey can involve many related requests

insights.claim: A member does not experience a traceId but a slow page, failed action, or unexpected feature behaviour, so linking experiences to backend systems gives a more direct path from user impact to technical cause.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: User-experience-centric observability is the value framing driving next-generation monitoring spend.
insights.quote: A member does not experience a traceId

insights.claim: LinkedIn uses OpenTelemetry as a common instrumentation, trace context, and semantic-convention model across mobile and web clients and backend services written in Java, Python, Go, and Rust.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Polyglot stacks are a key reason enterprises standardise on vendor-neutral OpenTelemetry.
insights.locator: LinkedIn operates a diverse technology stack

insights.claim: LinkedIn wraps and extends the standard OpenTelemetry SDKs so product teams get consistent instrumentation while the platform handles mobile lifecycle, export, and LinkedIn-specific metadata, with shared HTTP and gRPC frameworks auto-instrumenting common request paths.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Platform-team wrappers around open standards reduce dependency on vendor agents.
insights.locator: LinkedIn has built its own wrappers

insights.claim: LinkedIn transports telemetry through Apache Kafka and stores it in ClickHouse, using pageForestId, traceId, and timestamps as correlation keys.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: ClickHouse gaining a flagship observability storage use case supports its positioning against commercial backends.
insights.quote: Telemetry is transported through Apache Kafka and stored in ClickHouse
insights.locator: Telemetry is transported through Apache Kafka

insights.claim: Capturing every span would generate an enormous amount of telemetry, making sampling fundamental to LinkedIn's architecture.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Telemetry volume and cost are the central economic constraint in observability.

insights.claim: LinkedIn uses coordinated head sampling keyed on a pseudonymised member identifier so related client and server activity receives a consistent sampling decision, preventing a client span from being kept while its backend trace is discarded or vice versa.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Consistent cross-tier sampling is a design pattern that cuts cost without losing end-to-end fidelity.

insights.claim: LinkedIn estimates that up to 90% of some backend tracing volume could potentially be treated as debug-level data rather than valuable quality-of-experience telemetry.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: If typical, most tracing volume is low-value, a pressure point on volume-priced observability vendors.
insights.quote: up to 90% of some backend tracing volume could potentially be treated as debug-level data

insights.claim: Because mobile apps can be suspended or terminated before telemetry is sent, LinkedIn batches spans but can flush telemetry when an app moves into the background.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Client-side tracing has distinct engineering constraints that generic backend tools do not address.

insights.claim: LinkedIn applies attribute allowlists, denylists, and redaction to traces because distributed traces can otherwise become an unintended channel for sensitive application or member information.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Privacy controls in telemetry pipelines are becoming a required feature for observability platforms.
insights.quote: distributed traces can otherwise become an unintended channel for sensitive application or member information

themes.theme: Build vs buy and vendor independence

insights.claim: Backend-focused tracing tools such as Jaeger and Grafana Tempo mainly follow requests across services, while commercial platforms like Datadog and New Relic already combine distributed tracing with real-user and application monitoring.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Maps the competitive landscape LinkedIn chose to build around rather than buy from.
insights.locator: Traditional distributed tracing tools such as

insights.claim: LinkedIn's approach is less about a capability commercial platforms lack and more about making OpenTelemetry the common foundation, giving it control of its observability stack and avoiding instrumentation dependence on any particular commercial backend.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Large enterprises self-hosting on OTel plus Kafka/ClickHouse is a disintermediation risk for commercial observability vendors.
insights.quote: avoids making application instrumentation dependent on a particular commercial backend
insights.locator: This also gives LinkedIn greater control
